But I say to you, Neither Salomon in al his glorie vvas araied as one of these. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=28}}† And if the grasse that to day is in the field, and to morovv is cast into the ouen, God so clotheth: hovv much more you O ye of litle faith! {{verse|chapter=12|verse=29}}† And you, doe not seeke vvhat you shal eate, or vvhat you shal drinke: and c {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''μὴ μετεωρίζεσθε''.}}∷ be not lifted vp on high. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=30}}† for al these things the nations of the vvorld doe seeke. but your father knovveth that you haue neede of these things. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=31}}† But seeke first the kingdom of God, and al these things shal be giuen you besides. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=32}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel for S. Francis de Paula April. 2. S. Paulinus Jun. 22. S. Nicolas Tolentinas. Sept. 10. And for some other Confessors not Bishops.}}b Feare not {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ It was litle at the begining, & is stil in comparison of al the reprobate: but in itself very great, as in the parable of the great tree that grew of the litle mustard seed. ''Mt. 13''.}}∷ litle flocke, for it hath pleased your father to giue you a kingdom. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=33}}† Sel the things that you possesse, and giue almes. {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 6, 20.''}}* Make to you purses that vveare not, treasure that vvasteth not, in heauen: vvhither the theefe approcheth not, neither doth the mothe corrupt. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=34}}† For {{sup|‖}} vvhere your treasure is, there vvil your hart be also.⊣ {{verse|chapter=12|verse=35}}† b {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel for a Confessor that is not a Bishop.}}Let your {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ To girde our loines, is to keepe chastitie and cõtinencie. ''Gregor. ho. 13''.}}∷ loynes be girded, and candles burning in your handes, {{verse|chapter=12|verse=36}}† and you like to men expecting their lord, when he shal returne from the mariage: that vvhen he doth come and knocke, forthvvith they may open vnto him. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=37}}† Blessed are those seruants, vvhom vvhen the Lord commeth, he shal finde vvatching. Amen I say to you, that he vvil gird him self, and make them sit dovvne, and passing vvil minister vnto them. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=38}}† And if he come in the second vvatch, and if in the third vvatch he come, and so finde, blessed are those seruants. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=39}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 24, 43.''}}* And this knovv ye, that if the housholder did knovv vvhat houre the theefe vvould come, he would watch verely, and vvould not suffer his house to be broken vp. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=40}}† Be you also ready: for at vvhat houre you thinke not, the Sonne of man vvil come.⊣

{{verse|chapter=12|verse=41}}† And Peter said to him, Lord, doest thou speake this parable to vs, or likevvise to al? {{verse|chapter=12|verse=42}}† And our Lord said, VVho (thinkest thou) is a faithful stevvard and vvise, vvhom the lord appointeth ouer his familie, to giue them in season their measure of vvheate? {{verse|chapter=12|verse=43}}† Blessed is that seruant, vvhom vvhen the lord commeth, he shal finde so doing. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=44}}† Verely I say to you, that ouer al things vvhich he possesseth, he shal appoint him. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=45}}† But if that seruant say in his hart, My lord is long a comming: and shal begin to strike the seruants and handmaides, and eate and drinke, and be drunke: {{verse|chapter=12|verse=46}}† the lord of that seruant shal come in a day that he hopeth not, and at an houre that he knovveth not, and shal deuide him, and shal appoint his portion with the infidels. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=47}}† And that<noinclude>{{rh|||seruant}}</noinclude>
